logwatch.title: Log watcher
logwatch.lede: Errors and security mistakes agnts found in your projects' logs, grouped by error. It reports them, or opens a ticket to fix them, as Settings say.
logwatch.emptyActive: Nothing needs your attention: no new errors or security problems in the logs.
logwatch.howSources: Add a log source: the address of your Loki, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch or Graylog, or a push token for Vector or Fluent Bit. Then pick the services to watch and the repositories each runs on.
logwatch.howModes: Settings → Log watcher decides what happens: Report (shown here and notified) or Open ticket. Automatic tickets are off until you turn them on.
logwatch.fixStarted: {key} opened: agnts is on it. You review the fix before anything is pushed.
logwatch.muted: Muted: no more notifications or tickets for it.
logwatch.statusHelp_open: Seen in the logs; below the threshold, or its category is off
logwatch.statusHelp_fixed: The fix merged; waiting to see it gone from the logs
logwatch.statusHelp_regression: In the logs again after the fix
logwatch.regressionNote: This came back after its fix merged.
logwatch.noReposNote: No repository is selected for this service, so it is only reported. Select its repositories to let agnts fix it:
logwatch.excerptSub: Redacted: secrets and personal data are hidden before anything is stored.
logwatch.noExcerpt: No excerpt kept (it is dropped 30 days after the finding is over).
logwatch.occurrencesSub: The last 20 batches it was seen in.
logwatch.sourcesLede: The logging systems agnts reads, by address (through your private network when the address is on one), and the push tokens your log shippers send with.
logwatch.sourceDrawerSub: agnts tests the connection before it saves.
logwatch.name: Name
logwatch.environmentHelp: Debug mode counts as a problem in production only.
logwatch.addressHelp: A public address must use https. An address on your private network (10.x, *.local) is reached through it; add the network in Workspace settings first.
logwatch.authSaved: Saved ({kind}); kept unless you change them.
logwatch.authHelp_loki: Use a read-only token. A multi-tenant Loki also needs the tenant (X-Scope-OrgID).
logwatch.authHelp_elasticsearch: Use a key with read access to the index pattern only.
logwatch.authHelp_opensearch: Use a user with read access to the index pattern only.
logwatch.authHelp_graylog: Create an access token for a user with the Reader role.
logwatch.selectorHelp: Optional: what all services share, such as the environment label.
logwatch.pollHelp: 15 seconds keeps findings within a minute; a large shared cluster may want 60.
logwatch.fieldsHelp: Test connection fills these in; change them only if it guessed wrong.
logwatch.traceUrlHelp: Optional. A link to a trace in Tempo, Jaeger or Grafana, with '{traceId}' where the id goes. Findings from logs that carry a trace id link to it.
logwatch.ca: CA certificate (PEM), for a private CA
logwatch.pushHelp: Your shipper sends to agnts with a token. agnts shows the token and ready Vector, Fluent Bit, Promtail and OpenTelemetry configuration once you add the source.
logwatch.servicesSub: Tick the services to watch and pick the repositories each runs on (several for a gateway). Without a repository a service is only reported.
logwatch.discovering: Looking for services in the logs…
logwatch.noServices: No services found yet. Add one by name below.
logwatch.tokenSub: Shown once: copy it into your shipper's configuration now. Making a new one stops the old one.
logwatch.watching: {n, plural, =0 {No services watched} one {# service} other {# services}}
logwatch.deleteBody: agnts stops reading it. Its findings stay.
logwatch.howPull: Loki, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch or Graylog: enter the address and read-only credentials. agnts reads new entries every 15 seconds, filtered to what its detectors look for.
logwatch.howPrivate: On your own network? Add it as a private network (WireGuard, OpenVPN or agnts-link) and enter the internal address.
logwatch.howPush: No logging system with an API? Add a push source and point Vector or Fluent Bit at agnts.
logwatch.settingsSub: What agnts does with the errors and security problems it finds in your logs.
logwatch.errorsModeHelp: Exceptions, panics and bursts of server errors.
logwatch.securityModeHelp: Secrets and personal data in logs, stack traces sent to clients, debug mode, attacks.
logwatch.alwaysLeaksHelp: A secret written to the logs is a live incident: notify it even when Security is off.
logwatch.minSeverityHelp: Findings below it are recorded, not reported or ticketed.
logwatch.thresholdHelp: A plain error acts after this many in an hour; panics, leaks and attacks act on the first one.
logwatch.attackAfterHelp: The same attack on one route this many times in 7 days opens a ticket to add rate limiting or lockout; 0 never.
logwatch.resolveAfterHelp: For logs without a deployed revision: a fixed finding is resolved after this many quiet days.
logwatch.digestHelp: One message a day instead of one per finding (high-severity leaks still come at once).
logwatch.triageHelp: A light model explains new findings (on the workspace's credits); 0 keeps the rules' titles.
logwatch.patternsHelp: One a line: category:severity name=regex, such as security:high billing-token=\S+
logwatch.overridesHelp: A service is reported only until it has repositories: select them under
logwatch.agentHelp: On a server without a logging system: run this next to your services. It follows the containers labelled agnts.watch=logs, reports crashes, OOM kills and failed health checks, and connects out to agnts only.
logwatch.otelHelp: Add this pipeline to the Collector configuration. It sends a copy of error logs only; your other pipelines stay as they are.
logwatch.otelSdk: Apps that export with an OpenTelemetry SDK and no Collector send every log; agnts keeps what it needs:
logwatch.authHelp_datadog: An application key with the logs_read_data scope is enough.
logwatch.authHelp_cloudwatch: An IAM user or role with logs:DescribeLogGroups and logs:FilterLogEvents only.
logwatch.authHelp_splunk: The management API (port 8089); a token of a user who can search the index.
logwatch.indexHelp_elasticsearch: Empty reads logs-*, filebeat-* and logstash-*.
logwatch.indexHelp_opensearch: Empty reads logs-*, filebeat-* and logstash-*.
logwatch.indexHelp_splunk: Empty searches every index the token may read.
logwatch.indexHelp_cloudwatch: Services are log groups; this narrows the list (/ecs/, /aws/lambda/).
logwatch.overridesRuleHelp: One a line: a service as source/service (prod-loki/api) or a repository as repo:name, then errors= and/or security= off, report or ticket. A service's line wins over its repository's.
